book.old: <LbSay size={18}>{t('Before the first note: how to sit, and how to hold your hands. Get these right, and every note after them is easier.', '첫 음을 치기 전에: 어떻게 앉고, 손을 어떻게 둘지 배워요. 이걸 잘 잡으면 그다음 모든 음이 쉬워져요.')}</LbSay>
book.new: <LbSay size={18}>{t('First, learn to sit and hold your hands. Then every note is easier.', '먼저 앉는 법과 손 모양을 배워요. 그러면 모든 음이 쉬워져요.')}</LbSay>

book.old: <>맞출 것은 두 가지예요: 높이와 거리. 팔뚝은 건반과 수평이고, 팔꿈치는 몸 바로 앞에 있어요.
book.new: <>두 가지를 맞춰요: 높이와 거리. 팔뚝은 건반과 수평, 팔꿈치는 몸 바로 앞.

book.old: <>Two things to set: how high and how far. Your forearm is level with the keys, and your elbows sit just in front of your body.
book.new: <>Set two things: how high and how far. Forearm level with the keys, elbows just in front of you.

book.old: <>팔꿈치가 몸 바로 앞에 오도록, 옆구리에서 주먹 하나만큼 떨어지게 의자를 앞뒤로 옮겨요.
book.new: <>팔꿈치가 몸 바로 앞에, 옆구리에서 주먹 하나만큼 떨어지게 의자를 앞뒤로 옮겨요.

book.old: <>Slide in or out until your elbows are just in front of you, about a fist away from your sides.
book.new: <>Slide in or out until your elbows are just in front of you, a fist from your sides.

book.old: <>손끝은 늘 피아노와 이어져 있지만, 일은 팔 전체가 해요: 위에서 손과 손가락을 이끌어요. 여섯 가지 동작을 이 순서대로, 큰 몸 부분부터 작은 부분까지 해요. 하나하나가 다음 동작을 준비해 줘요.
book.new: <>손끝은 피아노와 이어져 있어요. 팔 전체가 위에서 손과 손가락을 이끌어요. 여섯 동작을 이 순서대로, 몸의 큰 부분부터 작은 부분까지. 하나하나가 다음 동작을 준비해요.

book.old: <>Your fingertips stay connected to the piano, but the whole arm does the work: from above, it leads the hand and the fingers. Six moves, in this order, from the big parts of the body to the small ones: each one gets the arm ready for the next.
book.new: <>The fingertips stay connected to the piano. The whole arm leads the hand and fingers from above. Six moves, in this order, big body parts to small. Each one sets up the next.

book.old: <LbRemember>{t('The arm leads from above, elbows free. Even while a finger presses a key, the whole arm stays free.', '팔이 위에서 이끌고, 팔꿈치는 자유롭게. 손가락이 건반을 누르는 동안에도 팔 전체는 자유로워요.')}</LbRemember>
book.new: <LbRemember>{t('The arm leads from above, elbows free. It stays free, even while a finger presses.', '팔이 위에서 이끌고, 팔꿈치는 자유롭게. 손가락이 누를 때도 팔은 자유로워요.')}</LbRemember>

book.old: <>팔을 늘어뜨렸다가, 작은 공을 쥐듯이 손을 들어 올려요. 손이 건반 위로 가도 그 모양 그대로예요. 손가락 마디는 다리처럼 위로, 손끝으로 쳐요. 손목은 자유롭게: 손끝을 건반에 댄 채로, 팔뚝 아래 롤러가 있는 것처럼 손이 위아래, 좌우로 흔들려요.
book.new: <>팔을 늘어뜨렸다가, 작은 공을 쥐듯 손을 들어요. 건반 위에서도 그 모양 그대로. 손가락 마디는 다리처럼 위로, 손끝으로 쳐요. 손목은 자유롭게: 손끝을 건반에 댄 채, 팔뚝 아래 롤러가 있듯 손이 위아래, 좌우로 흔들려요.

book.old: <>Let your arms hang, then lift your hands as if you were holding a small ball. Keep that shape when the hand goes on the keys. Knuckles up like a bridge, and play on the fingertips. The wrist stays free: with the fingertip on the key, the hand can sway up and down and side to side, as if a roller sat under your forearm.
book.new: <>Let your arms hang, then lift your hands as if holding a small ball. Keep that shape on the keys. Knuckles up like a bridge. Play on the fingertips. A free wrist: tip on the key, the hand sways up and down and side to side, as if on a roller under the forearm.

book.old: <>손가락마다 건반 하나씩, 손끝으로 쳐요. 마디는 위로 그대로, 나머지 손가락은 자기 건반 위에서 균형을 잡아요.</>
book.new: <>손가락마다 건반 하나씩, 손끝으로 쳐요. 마디는 위로. 나머지 손가락은 자기 건반에서 균형을 잡아요.</>

book.old: <>손끝을 건반에 대고: 롤러 위에 있는 것처럼 손목을 위아래로, 그다음 좌우로 흔들어요. 마디와 손끝을 살펴보고, 무너지지 않게 해 봐요.</>
book.new: <>손끝을 건반에 대고, 롤러 위처럼 손목을 위아래로, 그다음 좌우로 흔들어요. 마디와 손끝이 무너지지 않게 살펴봐요.</>

book.old: <>Play one key with each finger, on the tip. The knuckles stay up, and the other fingers rest on their keys to keep the balance.</>
book.new: <>Play one key with each finger, on the tip. Knuckles stay up. The other fingers rest on their keys for balance.</>

book.old: <>Fingertip on a key: sway the wrist up and down, then side to side, as if on a roller. Notice the knuckles and the tip, and try not to let them cave in.</>
book.new: <>Fingertip on a key: sway the wrist up and down, then side to side, as if on a roller. Watch the knuckles and tip so they don't cave in.</>

book.old: <LbRemember>{t('A free wrist, as if on a roller. Keep an eye on the knuckles and fingertips.', '롤러 위에 있는 것처럼 자유로운 손목. 마디와 손끝을 살펴봐요.')}</LbRemember>
book.new: <LbRemember>{t('A free wrist, as if on a roller. Watch the knuckles and fingertips.', '롤러 위처럼 자유로운 손목. 마디와 손끝을 살펴봐요.')}</LbRemember>

book.old: <>손가락마다 번호가 있어요. 엄지부터 1번에서 5번까지예요. 양손이 똑같아요: 두 엄지는 1번, 두 새끼손가락은 5번이에요.
book.new: <>손가락 번호는 엄지부터 1번에서 5번까지예요. 양손이 같아요: 두 엄지는 1번, 두 새끼손가락은 5번.

book.old: <>Every finger has a number, 1 to 5, starting from the thumb. It's the same on both hands: both thumbs are 1, and both little fingers are 5.
book.new: <>Fingers are numbered 1 to 5, from the thumb. Same on both hands: thumbs are 1, little fingers are 5.

book.old: {LANG === 'ko' ? <>앉은 자세, 둥근 손으로 쳐 봐요. 작게 시작해요: 한 음, 그다음 두 음, 세 음, 네 음, 다섯 음. 건반에서 건반으로 손이 작은 무지개를 그려요: 꽉 쥐지 않고 편하게, 손 전체가 도와줘요. 동그라미 하나가 일정한 박 하나예요.
book.new: {LANG === 'ko' ? <>앉은 자세, 둥근 손으로 쳐 봐요. 작게 시작해요: 한 음, 두 음, 세 음, 네 음, 다섯 음. 건반에서 건반으로 손이 작은 무지개를 그려요. 꽉 쥐지 말고 편하게, 손 전체가 도와줘요. 동그라미 하나가 일정한 박 하나예요.

book.old: <>Now put it together: sit well, make a round hand, and play. Start small: one note, then two, three, four, and all five. From key to key, the hand draws a little rainbow: relaxed, never squeezed tight, the whole hand helping. One circle is one steady beat.
book.new: <>Sit well, make a round hand, and play. Start small: one note, then two, three, four, five. Key to key, the hand draws a little rainbow. Relaxed, never squeezed: the whole hand helps. One circle is one steady beat.

book.old: {t('An empty dashed circle means: hold the note for one more beat.', '빈 점선 동그라미는 그 음을 한 박 더 누르고 있으라는 뜻이에요.')}
book.new: {t('An empty dashed circle: hold the note one more beat.', '빈 점선 동그라미: 그 음을 한 박 더 누르고 있어요.')}

book.old: <LbSay>{t('At the piano, before you play, every time, tick how each one is going: not yet, nearly, or got it! The check-up on paper is in the Workbook.', '피아노 앞에서, 칠 때마다, 치기 전에 먼저, 하나씩 어떤지 표시해요: 아직, 거의, 됐어요! 종이 점검은 워크북에 있어요.')}</LbSay>
book.new: <LbSay>{t('Every time, before you play, tick each one: not yet, nearly, or got it! The paper check-up is in the Workbook.', '칠 때마다, 치기 전에 하나씩 표시해요: 아직, 거의, 됐어요! 종이 점검은 워크북에 있어요.')}</LbSay>

guide.old: Before the first note: how to sit, and how to hold the hand. Get these two right and every note after them is easier, and kinder to the body.
guide.new: Before the first note, learn to sit and hold the hand. Get these right and every note is easier, and kinder to the body.

guide.old: Two things to set: how high the stool is, and how far it is from the keys. Then sit tall, like a puppet on a string.
guide.new: Set the stool's height and distance. Then sit tall, like a puppet on a string.

guide.old: • Distance: the elbows sit just in front of you and away from your body, about a fist from your sides.
guide.new: • Distance: the elbows sit just in front of you, a fist from your sides.

guide.old: The fingertips stay connected to the piano, but the whole arm does the work: from above, it leads the hand and the fingers, with the elbows free and away from the body. Even while a finger presses a key, the whole arm stays free.
guide.new: The fingertips stay connected to the piano. The whole arm leads the hand and fingers from above, elbows free and away from the body. It stays free even while a finger presses a key.

guide.old: Six moves, in this order, from the big parts of the body to the small ones: each one gets the arm ready for the next. A few minutes at the start of practice.
guide.new: Six moves, in this order, big body parts to small. Each one gets the arm ready for the next. A few minutes at the start of practice.

guide.old: Flop forward and let both arms hang heavy. Shake them loose, then float the hands up and set them gently on the keys.
guide.new: Flop forward, arms heavy. Shake them loose, then float the hands up and set them gently on the keys.

guide.old: Check the elbows are free, not stuck to the body: let them float out like wings, then back. Stop in the middle, a fist from the body.
guide.new: Elbows free, not stuck to the body: float them out like wings, then back. Stop in the middle, a fist from the body.

guide.old: Now the whole arm: skate along the keys. The round hand rides on the arm to the next group of keys. The fingers ride, they don't walk.
guide.new: The whole arm skates along the keys. The round hand rides on it to the next group of keys. The fingers ride, they don't walk.

guide.old: As the key goes down, a balloon lifts the wrist straight back up to level. The wrist never sinks, and the fingertip stays on the key.
guide.new: As the key goes down, a balloon lifts the wrist straight back up to level. It never sinks. The fingertip stays on the key.

guide.old: Let the arms hang, then lift the hands as if holding a small ball. That round shape is the one to keep on the keys.
guide.new: Let the arms hang, then lift the hands as if holding a small ball. Keep that round shape on the keys.

guide.old: • A free wrist: with the fingertip on the key, the hand can sway up and down and side to side, as if a roller sat under the forearm.
guide.new: • A free wrist: tip on the key, the hand sways up and down and side to side, as if on a roller under the forearm.

guide.old: • One plays, the others balance: one finger at a time goes down into its key, and the others rest on their keys and keep the hand balanced.
guide.new: • One plays, the others balance: one finger at a time goes into its key. The others rest on their keys.

guide.old: • Thumb in and out: check the thumb is free. It slides in under fingers 2, 3 and 4 and back out, while the hand stays round and still.
guide.new: • Thumb in and out: a free thumb slides in under fingers 2, 3 and 4 and back out. The hand stays round and still.

guide.old: The thumb seen from the front of the keyboard: it bends in, and the side of its tip touches the key. In light coral, where it goes when it slides in under the fingers, before it comes back out.
guide.new: The thumb from the front of the keyboard: it bends in, and the side of its tip touches the key. Light coral shows where it slides in under the fingers.

guide.old: The key is played with the soft middle of the finger. Try: hold a small ball, or a mandarin, and put that round shape on the keys.
guide.new: The soft middle of the finger plays the key. Try: hold a small ball or a mandarin, and put that round shape on the keys.

guide.old: The bridge has fallen in, lower than the wrist. Try: the knuckle bridge warm-up, with the knuckles staying up.
guide.new: The bridge has fallen in, lower than the wrist. Try: the knuckle bridge warm-up.

guide.old: The last joint bends backwards as the finger plays. Notice it: play slowly on the tip, press down and hold, and feel it stay firm, like a little pillar.
guide.new: The last joint bends backwards as the finger plays. Notice it: play slowly on the tip, hold, and feel it stay firm, like a little pillar.

guide.old: Every finger has a number, 1 to 5, starting from the thumb. It's the same on both hands, so both thumbs are 1 and both little fingers are 5. Teachers say "put finger 2 on D" all the time, so the numbers need to be automatic before reading fingering on the page.
guide.new: Fingers are numbered 1 to 5, from the thumb. Same on both hands: thumbs are 1, little fingers are 5. Teachers say "put finger 2 on D" all the time. The numbers must be automatic before reading fingering on the page.

guide.old: Now put it together: sit well, make a round hand, and play. Start small: one note, then two, three, four, and all five. From key to key the hand draws a little rainbow: relaxed, never squeezed tight, the whole hand helping.
guide.new: Sit well, make a round hand, and play. Start small: one note, then two, three, four, five. From key to key the hand draws a little rainbow. Relaxed, never squeezed: the whole hand helps.

guide.old: One circle is one steady beat; an empty dashed circle holds the note for one more beat.
guide.new: One circle is one steady beat. An empty dashed circle holds the note one more beat.

guide.old: Move the stool until every check turns green, do the six warm-ups with a moving picture of each, play the finger walks along with a steady beat, and play "Which finger?" on both hands.
guide.new: Move the stool until every check turns green, do the six warm-ups with moving pictures, play the finger walks to a steady beat, and play "Which finger?" on both hands.

guide.old: High enough that the forearm is level with the keys. If the feet then don't reach the floor, put a footstool or a sturdy box under them rather than lowering the stool.
guide.new: High enough that the forearm is level with the keys. If the feet don't reach the floor, put a footstool or sturdy box under them. Don't lower the stool.

guide.old: Neither: level with the forearm, and free, as if on a roller. After each key goes down, it comes straight back up to level instead of sinking.
guide.new: Neither: level with the forearm, and free, as if on a roller. After each key it comes straight back to level, never sinking.

guide.old: Close enough that the elbows sit just in front of the body, away from your sides by about a fist. Squashed elbows mean too close; arms reaching out mean too far.
guide.new: Close enough that the elbows sit just in front of the body, a fist from your sides. Squashed elbows mean too close. Arms reaching out mean too far.
